message.abstract: <jats:p>Accurate wind power prediction is essential for the efficient operation and maintenance of wind farms. However, achieving high-precision forecasting remains challenging due to complex, non-linear dynamics and the frequent neglect of spatiotemporal correlations among turbines and broader atmospheric influences. This study proposes the Graph-based External-context Adaptive Temporal Transformer (GEAT-Former), a physics-constrained dual-branch spatiotemporal graph neural network. The framework integrates three core components: a multi-source feature gating fusion module, a dual-stream graph attention architecture, and a physics-informed loss function. Specifically, the fusion module adaptively harmonizes internal operational data with exogenous meteorological fields. Within the dual-stream heterogeneous encoder, internal wind farm dynamics are captured via a synergistic dual-graph strategy: a static geographic graph characterizes inherent spatial topologies, while a dynamic feature graph models time-varying wake effects. Simultaneously, a spatial correlation graph utilizing Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) extracts the evolution of the surrounding meteorological field. A learnable adaptive gating mechanism further weighs the relative importance of microscopic information flow against macroscopic environmental contexts. Finally, a physics-informed loss function, grounded in aerodynamic principles, enforces the physical coupling between wind speed and power output to enhance predictive consistency. Evaluated on datasets from two commercial wind farms, GEAT-Former demonstrates superior performance, achieving an average Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) reduction of 27.08% compared to state-of-the-art baselines. These results underscore the efficacy of integrating dual-stream architectures with physical constraints for robust modeling under complex wind conditions.</jats:p>
title: Physics-Informed dual-branch graph neural network for wind farm cluster power forecasting
